bounds.domain: One shown-position request, two filter refresh/replacement generations and two view retirements; three ordered storage chunks with one pending call, one retirement and success/refusal/unknown acknowledgements; two one-shot operation owners, one independent refresh/query with explicit complete, truncated and unknown completeness, and whole-selection count classes0/100/101/1200. One optional external-open routing decision, one view retirement and five typed port reply classes.
bounds.authority: The host supplies active-view/storage permission and selected-document grants. A shown position binds the existing displayed filter generation and row array across access/selection waits. No file name is newly sent to the model. Existing direct path selection and owner-reviewed mutation contracts remain unchanged.
bounds.outcomes: Only confirmed chunk outcomes are counted and offered for Undo. Unknown later calls may have committed and are never automatically retried or included in confirmed Undo. Retiring a visit fences later chunk admissions, not effects already admitted. A later user Undo is a fresh operation. Partial/failed searches never claim complete or empty results. Filters persist until explicitly cleared; no age deadline is added.
bounds.conformance: Mandatory hook runs all63 existing owning Node cases with exact per-file/class/name identities and zero skips, including malformed/retired external fallback grants, complete file/folder forwarding and actual ZIP construction/CRC/byte decoding beyond100 selections and folders, truthful bounded-folder traversal and zero/500-row missing-completeness responses, plus all5 actual assistant schema/validation cases in a separate Vitest process. Held storage ports exercise actual production adapter methods, cancellation and independently settling operations.
bounds.limits: Partial source-linked projection, not universal refinement. Storage/file bytes are abstract in Quint; concrete ZIP checks use controlled entries and actual archive implementation. IndexedDB transaction races, arbitrary filesystem/provider identity changes without a delivered refresh, native permissions/intent limits, external renderer/accept commit behavior, physical device UI, network/storage availability, arbitrary collection sizes and multi-process ownership remain outside this model. Missing native query completeness is refused while retaining returned rows; hosts must explicitly report false only for complete queries. Host-owned external opening does not prove another application consumed the file.
bounds.progress: Named weak fairness yields local settlement despite failure or unknown outcomes. Required no-fairness counterexamples retain possible waits. No fairness assumes a successful provider call or that cancellation undoes admitted effects.

assumptions: Weak fairness of the explicitly named local completion/dispatch actions. A port may fail or have an unknown outcome; provider success and wall-clock deadlines are not assumed.
No fairness: a pending host/storage receipt or continuation may stutter forever.
